chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a slave belonging to a man who fled from him and went to a land. There he told them that he was a free man from the clan of Banu so-and-so, and that he married a woman from the people of that land and she bore him children. Then the woman died and left in his hand wealth, landed property, and her children. After that, his master came to that land, took the slave and all that was in his hand, and the slave admitted to him that he was in bondage.
So he said: "As for the slave, he is his slave; and as for the wealth and the landed property, they belong to the children of the deceased woman. A slave does not inherit from a free person."

I said: "May I be your ransom, if the woman had no child and no heir on the day she died, then to whom would the wealth and landed property that she left in the hand of the slave belong?" He said: "All that she left belongs exclusively to the Imam of the Muslims."

key_terms.أَبَقَ: fled from his master as a runaway slave
key_terms.إِمَامِ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Imam who holds authority over the communal estate when no private heir exists
key_terms.وَارِثٌ: a legal heir entitled to inheritance
key_terms.يَرِثُ: inherits legally from a deceased person

ai.seo_question: If an escaped slave possesses the estate of his deceased free wife, who legally inherits it in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an escaped slave who falsely claimed freedom, married, and held property after his wife's death. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام rules that the slave remains the property of his master, while the deceased free woman's estate goes to her children, since a slave does not inherit from a free person. If she leaves no heir, her estate belongs exclusively to the Imam of the Muslims.
